text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The decision by the ruling Kenya African National Union (KANU) party to establish a commission to review the constitution draws mixed reaction from the opposition and clergymen who call it suspect.
- Two days after a visit by Rwandan vice-president Paul Kagame Kenyan police round up seven Rwandan Hutus and hand them over to the U.N.'s Rwanda genocide tribunal.
- The Organisation of African Unity (OAU) has pledged assistance to Kenya as it grapples with reforming its constitution.
- An interdenominational funeral service is held in Nairobi's central Uhuru Park for 14 victims of July 7 violence. The dead are eulogised as heroes whose blood was not shed in vain.
- KANU's suprise move to set up a commission to review the constitution is welcomed in some quarters and rejected in others.
- A judge suggests that child defilers and rapists be jailed for life to deter other would-be rapists.
- Pro-reformists and opposition groups appear caught off guard by KANU's bold offensive to initiate reforms ahead of the impending elections.
- President Moi restates his commitment to constitutional reforms and adds any changes must be aimed at uniting Kenyans.
- National Development Party leader Raila Odinga differs with his closest ally FORD-Kenya chairman Kenneth Matiba over the leadership of the opposition-proposed constitutional reforms conference.
